setup_scripts:
-c import sys, os
sys.path.insert(0, '.')
os.makedirs('instance', exist_ok=True)
from app import create_app, db
from app.models.user import User, UserRole
from app.models.whitelist import Whitelist
app = create_app()
ctx = app.app_context()
ctx.push()
db.create_all()
def ensure(xuid, username, password, role):
    u = User.query.filter_by(xuid=xuid).first()
    if not u:
        u = User(); u.xuid = xuid; u.username = username; u.role = role; u.set_password(password)
        db.session.add(u); db.session.flush()
    if not Whitelist.query.filter_by(xuid=xuid).first():
        w = Whitelist(); w.xuid = xuid; w.username = username; w.whitelisted_by = None
        db.session.add(w)
    db.session.commit()
    return u
admin = ensure('TESTXUID001', 'AdminTester', 'AdminPass123!', UserRole.ADMIN)
staff = ensure('TESTXUID002', 'StaffTester', 'StaffPass123!', UserRole.STAFF)
print('seeded admin id=', admin.id, 'staff id=', staff.id)

applications.why_selected: Real Flask + Flask-SQLAlchemy staff/tournament management app for a Minecraft server community, MIT licensed. update_role() does a genuine admin-gated, persisted role change (staff / manager / admin) with a real self-demotion guard and a real access-control check rejecting non-admins -- all logic entirely self-contained (no external API dependency). Real account creation/whitelisting DOES require a live third-party NetherGames Minecraft API call this sandbox cannot and should not depend on, so two real accounts are seeded directly via the app's own real User/Whitelist models and set_password() (the same class of setup already used for CasettaFit's admin seed) -- update_role() itself is exercised entirely through its own real HTTP route, unmodified.
